input.question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?
input.ground_truth: F-35 is pretty much 3 different planes, that look similar. * Navy version has different wings and modifications to frame to support carrier landing. * Marine version has VSTOL. * Air Force version has better performance.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friend both want to build a really cool toy car. You want yours to do lots of different tricks, like fly, swim, and even drive on land. Your friend just wants a super fast race car that only goes on the track.

Now, your toy car has to be made so it can do all those tricks, so you have to use lots and lots of different parts and make sure it works in many different ways. That means you have to try it over and over, fix things, and make sure it’s safe. All of that takes a lot of time and money.

Your friend’s car is just for racing, so it’s simpler. But maybe your friend also wants the car to look super cool and have lots of colors and lights, and wants to change the design a lot while building it. That also makes it take longer and cost more.

The F-35 is like your super trick car. It was supposed to be used by three different countries, so it had to be made in a way that lots of people could use it, and it had to do many different jobs. That made it really complicated and expensive to build, even though some of the technology inside isn’t as fancy as the F-22’s.

The F-22 is like the fast race car. It was only made for one country and was built to do one really special job: fly really fast and be hard to see. But even though it has some very advanced tricks, it didn’t have to change as much to please different people.

So, even if the F-35 isn’t as “high tech” in some ways, having to do so many things and please so many people made it much more expensive to build.
